issues.description: The problem statement (UML and instructions) requires public getters for all attributes of ExcellenceLand, including the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough' (which implies a boolean-returning getter such as boolean isExcellentEnough()). In the solution, the getter for 'excellentEnough' is declared as public String isExcellentEnough() and returns "Yes"/"No" instead of returning a boolean. This changes the method return type and semantics and contradicts the specified attribute type and the requirement to provide standard getters. Students following the specification will expect a boolean getter and will be confused or prevented from matching tests that expect a boolean-returning getter.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the getter in the solution to return the boolean attribute directly. For example, declare public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } (or public boolean getExcellentEnough()) so the getter's return type matches the 'excellentEnough' boolean attribute and the UML/instruction expectations.
